scripts.verify: pnpm format:check && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm verify:contract && pnpm prop-map:check && pnpm adr-index:check && pnpm verify:docs && pnpm verify:figma && pnpm build && pnpm test

pnpm.//typescript: PINNED WITH A TILDE ON PURPOSE. Under typescript@6.x, react-docgen-typescript stops classifying VariantProps-derived props as enums: the literal value arrays come back empty and every contract answer silently thins out. docgen's peer range is '>= 4.3.x', so nothing warns you. Do not widen this to ^5 or ^6 without re-running the extraction check and reading the report.

//typescript: Tilde-pinned, and THE REASON IT WAS PINNED IS GONE. It protected react-docgen-typescript, which silently stopped classifying VariantProps-derived props as enums under typescript@6 — value arrays came back empty and every contract answer thinned out with nothing warning you. That library and the extraction readers that used it were deleted on 2026-09-03, because components are generated from contracts and there is no hand-written source left to read. So this pin now defends nothing measurable. It is left in place because widening a toolchain range is a deliberate act with its own blast radius, not a side effect of deleting dead code — but whoever wants typescript 6 should now simply take it.
